translations.text: Three years after the fall of the city, I, Salathiel, who is Ezra, was in Babylon. I lay troubled on my bed, my eyes were lifted up, and thoughts came into my heart,
for I saw the desolation of Zion and the building up of those who lived in Babylon.
My spirit was greatly stirred, and I began to speak to the Most High with fearful words,
and I said: "O Lord! In the beginning, when you alone made the earth, you commanded it,
and it brought forth the lifeless body of Adam. He too was the work of your hands. You breathed a living spirit into him, and he became alive before you.
You brought him into paradise, which your right hand had planted before the earth was set in order.
You gave him your truth as a command. But he disobeyed you, and at once you laid death on him and on all his descendants. From him came offspring and tribes, peoples and nations without number.
Each of those nations walked according to its own will. They acted wickedly before you and rejected you, but you did not stop them.
Then in time you brought the flood upon the earth and upon those who lived on the earth, and you destroyed them.
Destruction came on all of them. As death came because of Adam, so the flood came upon them.
But you saved one of them together with his household, and from him came many righteous people.
Then the inhabitants of the earth began to multiply on the earth. Their offspring, peoples and descendants grew very many, and they began to act more wickedly than those who came before.
While they were acting wickedly before you, you chose one of them, whose name was Abraham.
You loved him and revealed yourself to him alone.
You made an everlasting covenant with him and said, 'I will not forsake your descendants.'
And you brought his descendants out of Egypt to Mount Sinai.
You bent down the heavens, moved the earth, and shook the ends of the earth. You made the depths tremble and terrified the world.

Your glory passed through the four gates of heaven: of earthquake, of the blowing wind, and of ice. It did this so that you might give the law to the descendants of Jacob and the truth to the tribe of Israel.
But you did not take the evil heart away from them, so that your law might bear fruit in them.
For the evil heart was first planted in Adam. He was overcome by it, and so were all his descendants with him.
So their weakness stayed. The law was in the people's heart together with the root of evil. The good turned away from them, and the evil stayed.
Many days passed and the times were completed. Then you raised up your servant David for yourself,
and you told him to build a city for your name and to offer your offerings in it.
After many years had passed, the people who lived in that city sinned against you.
They did nothing new. They did what Adam did, as all his descendants did, for the same evil heart had been planted in them too.
And you gave that city into the hands of your enemies.
And then I said in my heart: Who knows? Perhaps the inhabitants of Babylon are doing something better, and that is why the city of Zion was given to them?
And it came to pass, when I came to Babylon, that I saw ungodliness without number, and my soul has seen many scorners for these three years, and my heart was amazed,
for how do you bear with sinners and spare the ungodly? You have destroyed your people and preserved your enemies, and you have made known to no one why their ways have fallen.
Or has Babylon done better than Zion, or any other nation? (32) Or who has known you more than Israel? Or what seed has believed your covenant as Jacob did?
Their reward has not appeared, and their labour has not brought forth fruit. For I have travelled about among the nations and seen them prospering, and they have not remembered your commandments.
Now, then, let us weigh in the balance our iniquities and the iniquities of the inhabitants of their world, and the beam of their balance has weighed down.
Or when have the inhabitants of the earth not sinned against you? Or what tribe has kept your commandments?
You will find individual men, by name, who have kept your commandments, but a nation you will not find.
And the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered me
and said to me: Your heart is utterly amazed, and you wish to attain to the glory of the Most High?
And I said: Yes, lord! He answered and said to me: I have been sent to you to show you three ways and to set three ways before you.
If you tell me one of them, I too will make known to you the way that your heart says it wants to see, and I will tell you where the evil heart comes from.
And I said: Speak, my lord! And he said to me: Go and weigh the flame of fire in a balance, or measure the winds with a measure, or call back and bring before me a day that has passed.
I answered and said: Who of those born could do this, that you ask me about it?

He answered and said to me: If I had asked you and said: 'How many treasuries are there in the heart of the sea? Or how many springs of the deep have there been from the beginning? Or how many places are there above the firmament? Or what are the exits of hell like? Or what are the entrances of the kingdom of heaven like?'
you might have answered me and said: 'I have not gone down into the deep, nor have I gone down into hell, nor have I gone up into heaven, nor have I seen paradise.'
But now I have asked you nothing except about fire and wind and the day that has passed, things you have passed through and without which you cannot exist, and you could not answer me about them.
I answered and said: I cannot understand that. And he said to me: You cannot know the things that have grown up with you;
how then can your head contain the ways of the Most High? The ways of the Most High were created beyond comprehension, and what is corruptible cannot understand the ways of the incorruptible.
And when I heard this, I fell on my face and said: It would have been better for us not to exist than to exist like this and live in ungodliness and suffering, without understanding why I suffer.
He answered and said to me: The tall trees of the field set out and took counsel
and said: 'Come, let us go and make war on the sea, so that it may retreat from us, and we may make for ourselves another forest there.'
And likewise the waves of the sea took counsel and said: "Come, let us rise up against the forests of the plain and make war on them, so that we may win that place for ourselves as well."
And the plan of the forest came to nothing, for fire came and burned them up;
and so did the plan of the waves of the sea, for the sand stood against them and stopped them.
If you were the judge, which of these would you declare in the right, and which would you put to shame?
I answered and said to him: Both made a useless plan, for the land has been given to the forest, and to the sea has been given a place in which to hold its waves.
He answered and said to me: You have judged well. Why then have you not been able to judge your own case?

For just as the land has been given to the forest and the sea to its waves, so also those who live on earth can understand only what belongs to the earth, and those who live in heaven what belongs to heaven.
But I answered and said: I beg you, O God, why have you given me a mind to think about these things?

For I do not wish to ask about the ways above, but about the affliction that keeps coming upon us: that Israel has been handed over to the gentiles, and the people you loved you have given to godless nations, and the law of our fathers has been brought to nothing, and the written covenants are nowhere to be seen.
And we pass from this world like locusts, and our life is like smoke, and we are not worthy to find mercy.
But what will become of his great name for us, the name by which we are called? This is why I am asking you.
He answered me and said to me: If you are still alive, you will see, and if you live on, you will understand fully: this world is hastening to pass away.
For it cannot contain or bear what has been promised to the many, because this world is filled with pain and full of grief.
For evil has been sown in it, but the harvest of what you asked me about has not yet come.
Unless it is first reaped, and the place where evil was sown is cleared away, the place where good was sown cannot come.

For the grain of evil seed was sown in Adam's heart from the beginning. Judge for yourself how much fruit of ungodliness it has produced up to now, and how much more it will produce until the threshing floor comes!
For a single grain, the seed of evil, has brought forth so much fruit of evil.
But when the ears of good seeds beyond number have been sown, how much greater will the harvest of the threshing floor be?
I answered and said: How long, Lord? When will this happen? For are our years few and evil?
He answered and said to me: You are not in more of a hurry than the Most High. For you hurry for your own sake, but the Most High for the sake of many.
Was it not about this that the souls of the righteous asked concerning their treasuries, saying: "How long are we to stay here? When will the threshing floor of our labor come?"
The angel Uriel answered them and said to them: "When that number of likeness is complete. For he has weighed this world in a balance,
and measured out the times by measure, and he will not quiet them or stir them up until the promised measure is fulfilled."
I answered and said: Yes, Lord. But now, look, we are all full of ungodliness.
And perhaps the threshing floor of the righteous is being held back because of us, or because of the sins of those who live on the earth.
He answered me and said to me: "Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when she has completed her nine months, her womb can still hold back what is coming out of it."
And I said: "It cannot, Lord!" And he said to me: "Hades and the treasuries of souls are like the womb.
For just as the womb hastens because of the pain of giving birth, so too the earth hastens to give back what has been entrusted to it from the beginning.
And then I will show you the vision of which your heart has spoken to you."
I answered and said to him: "If I have found favor in your eyes, and if you think it right, and if I am able,
show me this too: are the times that have passed more, or are those that are still to pass more?
For I know what has passed, but I do not know what is still to pass."
And he said to me: "Stand at my right, and I will show you the explanation of a parable."
And I saw this: a furnace was burning before me, and when the flame had passed, I looked, and smoke remained from it.
And after that a cloud full of rain passed before me, and it let down a very violent rain; and when that heavy [?] rain had passed, only drops remained from it.

And he said to me: "Weigh it for yourself: just as the rain is more than those drops, and the fire more than the smoke, so the times that have passed are greater; and what still remains is like that smoke and those drops."
I answered with entreaty and said to him: "Lord, will I still be alive until that day? Or what will happen in those days?"
He answered me and said to me: "About the signs you asked me about, I will tell you in part; but about your life I have not been sent to tell you, nor indeed do I know.
As for the sign: behold, days are coming when great terror will seize the inhabitants of the earth; and then the portion of truth will be hidden, and the place of faith will be barren.
Falsehood will increase, and the royal lands that you now see will become a desolate wilderness,
and people will see the land as a wilderness.
If the Most High grants you life, you will see an uprising after the third day, and suddenly the sun will shine out at night and the moon by day.
And blood will drip from wood, and stone will give out its voice, and peoples will be shaken, and the airs will be changed.
And the one in whom they did not believe will reign,
and all will hear his voice.
And many places will split open, and fire will be sent upon them again and again. And the beasts of the field will leave their land, and portents will be born from women.
And sweet waters will turn salty, and friends will fight one another; and then wisdom will be hidden from them, and knowledge will withdraw into its treasury.
And people will seek it among many and will not find it, and sin and wickedness will increase on the earth.

And one land will ask another land, and neighbor will ask neighbor, and say: 'Has righteousness, or a righteous person, passed through from there?' But the other will deny it and say: 'I do not know.'
And at that time people will hope to find, but will not attain; they will marry, but will not be content in their homes, and their labor will not prosper.
These are the signs I was allowed to tell you. If you pray and weep again, as you are doing now, and fast for seven more days, you will hear greater signs.
When I woke up, my body trembled violently, and my soul was fainting from exhaustion.
Then the angel who had come to me and was speaking with me took hold of me. He strengthened me and set me on my feet.
On the second night Phaltiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said to me: "Where have you been, and why is your face sorrowful?
Do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the land of their exile?
Get up now, break your fast and eat some food, so that you do not abandon us, like a shepherd who leaves his flock in the hands of a wicked wolf."
I answered him and said: "Go away, and do not come to me for seven days. After that, come to me, so that I may tell you something." And he went away from me.
So I fasted for seven days, mourning and weeping, as the angel Uriel had commanded me.
After those seven days, the thoughts of my heart came back and troubled me greatly.
My heart received the spirit of understanding, and I began to speak again before the Most High.
I said: "Lord God, out of all the forests of the earth and all its trees, you have chosen a vine for yourself.
Out of all the places of the world, you have chosen one floor for yourself, and out of all the flowers, the lily.
Out of all the depths of the earth and the seas, you have made one river great for yourself, the Jordan. Out of all the cities that have been built, you have made Zion holy for yourself.
Out of all the created birds of the sky, you have given a name to one dove for yourself. Out of all the sheep you have created, you have been pleased with one sheep for yourself.
Out of all the peoples you have made, you have made one people, Israel, [?] your own. And out of all the tested nations, you have graciously given the law to the people whom you loved.
So now, Lord, why have you handed that one people over to the many? You have dishonored that one root above all other roots, and you have scattered your only-begotten among all the nations.
Those who oppose your law have trampled down those who believe in your law.
If you truly hate your people, they ought to be punished by your own hands."
While I was still speaking these words, the same angel who had come to me on the first night was sent again.
He said to me: "Listen to me and I will tell you. Pay attention to me, and I will tell you more."
I said: "Speak, Lord!" He answered me and said: "Are you so deeply troubled about Israel? Or do you love Israel more than its own Creator does?"
I said: "No, Lord. But I grieve for Israel, and I speak because my inmost being torments me every hour, and I want to understand the ways of the Most High and to search out his judgment."

He answered me and said: "You cannot." I said: "Why can I not, Lord? Then why was I created? Why did my mother's womb not become my grave, so that I would not have seen the suffering of Jacob and the affliction of the race of Israel?"
He said to me: "Count for me the times that have not yet come. Gather the scattered drops of rain, and bring back the color of a withered flower.
Open for me the closed chambers of the treasuries, and bring out for me the winds [or: spirits] that are shut up [?] there, and show me the face,
And I said: Lord, who is able to see this, except one whose dwelling is not among men?
But I am foolish and poor. How could I tell of the thing you are asking me about?
And he said to me: Just as you cannot do even one of the things that were mentioned, so you cannot work out or reach my judgment, nor the love of the end that I have kept in store for my people.
I answered and said to him: Yes, Lord, you have kept it in store for the perfect. But what will they do, those who went before us, or we, or those who come after us?
And he said to me: I will liken my judgment to a crown. It is not only for the last, who lag behind, nor only for the first, who hasten ahead.
I answered and said to him: Lord, could you not have [made] all at once those who have been, those who are, and those who are to be, so as to show your judgment more quickly?
He answered and said to me: Judgment could not hasten ahead of the Creator. Nor could this world have borne it if those created upon it had been created all at once.

I answered and said to him: You told your servant that you will raise up together, by resurrection, what was created by you from nature [?]. If you will give life to them all at once and creation will bear it, then it could also bear now those who are [to be] all at once.
He answered and said to me: Ask a woman's womb and say to it: "If you are to bear ten, why do you bear them one at a time?" Beg it to give birth to all ten at once.
But it cannot do so. It can only give birth one at a time.
For I have made the earth a womb for those who come forth from it.
For just as a child that has not [yet] been born cannot grow old, so I have ordered this world that I created.
I answered and asked him: Lord, since you have opened a way for me to speak, I will begin to speak before you. Is our mother, of whom you spoke, still young, or is she now reaching old age?
He answered and said to me: Ask a woman who gives birth
and say to her: "Why are those you bear now not equal to the first ones, but smaller in stature?"
She will answer you and say: "The strength of those born in youth is one thing, and the strength of old age is another."
In the same way, understand that those of the present are weaker in strength than those who came first,
and those who come after you will be weaker than you, since this present life is different from that of youth.
And I said: I beg you, Lord, if I have found favour in your eyes, make known to your servant for whom you intend your judgment.

He answered and said to me: The beginning is for man, but the end is for me. For it was as at the first: before the ground of the earth was made, before the outlets of this world were established, before the balance of the winds went forth;
before the thunder roared, before the stars shone forth, before the foundation of paradise was laid;
before the beauty of the flowers sprang up, before the firmness of the powers was made strong, before the countless hosts of angels were set apart;
before the heights of the air were raised up, before the measure of the firmament was named, before the foundation of Zion was laid;
before the years of this world were searched out, before the ways of sinners were made, before the treasures stored up for the faithful were sealed.
Then I took counsel, and it came into my heart, for me alone and not for another.
I answered and said to him: "And what will the sign of those times be? How near will the end be? And how will the beginning of the second age be?"
And he said to me: "From Adam until Abraham, for from him were born Jacob and Esau.
The beginning of the coming age is Jacob.
For the end of a man is the heel, and the beginning of a man is the hand. Between the heel and the hand seek nothing, O Ezra!"
I answered and said to him: "O Lord God, if I have found grace in your eyes,
show me the sign of the end, which you showed me in part on the first night."
He answered and said to me: "Stand up on your feet, and you will hear a voice full of completeness.
And then the place on which you stand will be shaken with a quaking.
Do not fall down at that word alone, for the word concerns the end, and the foundation of the earth will understand.
For that saying is about the earth: it will tremble and be shaken and know that it is to be changed at the end."
And as soon as I heard this, I stood up on my feet, and behold, I heard the voice of speech, like the roar of many waters.
And it said to me: "Behold, the days are coming, and it will be that when I intend to draw near and visit the inhabitants of the earth,
and when I intend to repay those who were harmed for the harm done by those who harmed them, and when the humiliation of Zion is brought to an end,
and when the coming age is sealed, I will make this sign: books will be opened before the face of the firmament, and all will see them together.
Year-old children will speak with their voices, and pregnant women will give birth to unformed children at three months and four months, and these will live and move about.
Fields will suddenly be found sown and sprouted, and full storehouses will be found empty.
The trumpet will sound with a loud voice, and all who hear it will fall down.

And in those times friends will fight one another like enemies, and the earth will grow faint together with its inhabitants, and the springs of water will be held back and will not flow for as long as three hours.
And everyone who is left after all these things, of which you spoke before, will be saved and will see my salvation and the end of this world of mine.
And then men will be seen who were taken up to heaven, who have not tasted death since their birth. The heart of the inhabitants of the earth will be changed, and will be turned into another mind.
For evil will be blotted out, and deceit will be extinguished.
Faith will flourish, corruption will be overcome, and truth will appear, which until now has been without fruit."
And while he was still saying this to me, the ground on which I stood began to shake.
And he said to me: "I came to tell you this during the night that has passed.
If you pray again and fast for seven days, I will tell you still more than this."
For your voice has indeed been heard before the Most High, and the Mighty One has seen your uprightness, which you have had since your youth.
Therefore he sent me to make all this known to you, and he said to me: "Be strong and do not be afraid,
and do not be in a hurry to understand evil concerning the former times, so that you are not terrified in the last times."
After this I wept again as before, and I fasted seven days, so that I might complete the seven days, as he had commanded me at first.
On that night my heart was again troubled within me, and I began to speak before the Most High,
for my spirit was burning greatly and my heart was growing faint [?].
I said: "O Lord God, you spoke by your word at the beginning of creation, on the first day, and said, 'Let there be heaven and earth,' and your word brought the works to completion.
For the spirit was then hovering, and darkness moved about in silence, and the sound of a human voice had not yet been heard.
Then you commanded that light be sent forth from your treasuries, so that your works might be made bright.
On the second day you then created the spirit of the firmament and commanded it to divide the waters, so that some of the waters would stand above and some would remain below.
On the third day you commanded the waters to gather into the seventh part of the earth, and you made six parts dry land before you, for service, for sowing, and for adornment.
For your word had only to go forth, and at once your work was done.

There was prepared, and there sprang up, a countless multitude of fruits, foods of many kinds pleasing to the taste, flowers of unmatched colour, beautiful and countless trees, and fragrances past searching out. All this you made on the third day.
On the fourth day you commanded the sun to shine forth, the moon to give light, and the stars to keep their changing order.
And you commanded them to serve the man whom you had purposed to create.
On the fifth day you commanded the seventh part, where the waters were, which is called the reservoir, to bring forth living creatures, birds and fish.
And that water, lifeless and speechless, became a bringer-forth of living things, so that because of this the generations might tell of your wonders.
Then you set apart and kept two living creatures from among those that had been created. One you named Behemoth, and the other you named Leviathan.
You separated them from each other, for the seventh part, the reservoir where the waters stood, could not hold [?]
To Behemoth you gave one part of the dry land, and on the third day [?], so that he might dwell on it, where there are four mountains.
But to Leviathan you gave the seventh part of the sea. You have kept them so that you may give them as food to whomever you wish.
On the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you cattle, wild beasts, and birds.
You set Adam over them as ruler, over all the works you had created before. From him we were later born, the people whom you chose.
I have dared to say this before you, O Lord, because you said, 'For your sakes I created this world.'
But the other nations, also born of Adam, are counted as nothing. They are reckoned as mere spittle from the mouth, and their wealth is like a drop from a cask.
And now, behold, O Lord, a contemptible nation rules over us with violence, holds dominion over us, and crushes us.
But we, your people, whom you called firstborn and only-begotten, treasured [?] and beloved, have now been given into their hands.
If you created this world for our sake, why have we not inherited the world? Or how long will it be so?
And when I had finished these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the first night appeared to me,
and said to me: "Arise, Ezra, and hear the words for which [?]"
And I said: "Speak, my lord." He answered and said to me: "If a sea lies in a wide place, and it is broad and great,
but its entrance is in a narrow place, no wider than a river,
if someone intends to enter that sea and see it, or to rule over it, will they not be unable to enter its broad part unless they pass through that narrow place?
Or if a city is built and stands on a plain, and is full of every good thing,
but the entrance to that city is narrow and steep, and on its right side there is fire and on its left deep water,
and between the two of them, the fire and the water, there is a single path, too narrow to hold [?], with room only for a man's foot to be set,
and if that city is given to some man as an inheritance, how will the heir take possession of his inheritance unless he first passes through that narrow and terrible place?"
And I said: "It is so, lord." And he said to me: "So also is the portion of Israel."
Truly I created this world for their sake; and when Adam transgressed my commandments, what had been made was judged.
And the entrances of this world became pain and toil: evil, few, full of much sorrow, multiplied with great affliction, and filled with toil.
But the entrances of the world to come are secure and broad, and yield untroubled fruit.
Unless the living pass through that narrow place and affliction, they cannot receive the good that is set before them.
But now you, why are you troubled, O mortal?
Or why have you not taken to heart the life of the world to come?"
I answered and said to him: "O Lord God, you have said in the law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the ungodly shall perish.
For the righteous will endure affliction well and hope for comfort, but the ungodly will not endure the narrowness, nor will they reach the broad places."
He answered and said to me: "You are not a judge apart from the Only One, nor are you wiser than the Most High.
Many of this world shall perish, because they despised the law of God.
For God gave commandment to the fathers in his presence, that they should do it and live, or that they should keep it and not be condemned.
But they became unbelieving and contentious, and devised evil thoughts of their own accord.
And they devised [?] schemes of sins, and on top of all this they did not know the Most High, and they perverted his ways,
and they ignored his law, and despised his commandments, and did not believe his law, and belittled his works.
And therefore empty things are for the empty, and full things for the full.
And behold, the time is coming when the sign that I told you of before will appear, and the city that is now seen [?] will be revealed, and the ground that has been measured out will appear.
And all who have been delivered from those former evil deeds will see my wonders.
For my chosen anointed one will be revealed, together with those who are with him, and he will gladden the remnant who have been saved for four hundred years.
And after those years my chosen anointed one will die, and all people who have breath.
And this world will be given over to the primeval silence for seven days, as at the first beginnings, until nothing at all remains.
And after those seven days the world that is not yet awake here will awaken, and corruption will pass away.
And it will give up those who are asleep in it, the peoples who rest in silence in it, and after this they will give back the souls that were entrusted to them.
And the Most High will be revealed on the throne of glory, and mercy will pass away, and they will turn away [?] compassion, and long-suffering will be withdrawn.
Only judgment will remain before him, and truth will stand forth with him, and faith will spring up.

And each person's deeds shall follow them, and the recompense of the reward shall appear. Righteous deeds shall awaken, and iniquities shall not sleep. The pit of judgment shall be opened, and opposite it the place of rest. The furnace of Gehenna shall appear, and opposite it the paradise of delight.

Then the Most High shall say to the nations that have been raised up: "See and know whom you denied, or whom you did not serve, or whose true commandments you despised. Look: before you is delight and rest on this side, and fire and torment on that side." This is what he will say to them on the day of judgment.

The day of judgment is like this. There shall be no sun, no moon, no stars, no clouds, no lightning, no thunder, no winds, no waters, no air. There shall be no darkness, no evening, no morning. There shall be no summer, no autumn, no winter, no spring [?], no heat, no frost, no cold, no hail, no rain, no dew. There shall be no day, no night, no dawn, no midday, no brightness, no light. There shall be only the splendours of the glory of the Most High, so that all may see what is before them. Its course shall last only up to seven years, that is, seven periods [?]. This is my judgment and its ordinances, and I have made this known to you alone.

I answered and said: "Lord, now again I say: blessed are those in this world who have kept your law. But this is what my prayer is about: who is there in this age [?] who has not sinned against you? Who has been born who has not broken your law? And now, as I see it, the joy of that world will be for a few, and torment for many. For an evil heart has been placed among us. It has led us astray and brought me to corruption. It has shown us the ways of death and destruction and taken us far from life. And this is not just a few, but practically all whom he has created."

He answered and said to me: "Listen to me and I will tell you, and then you will understand. This is why the Most High made not one world only, but two. You said that the righteous will be not many, but few compared with the others. Then mix clay and lead into a vessel."

And I said: "That I cannot do, Lord."

And he said to me: "Not only that. Ask the earth and it will tell you; speak with it and it will inform you. Say to it: 'You bring forth gold and silver and bronze and iron and lead and clay. Iron is more plentiful than silver, lead more than bronze, and clay more than iron.' Weigh for yourself which is more precious and desirable: what is plentiful, or what is found rarely?"

And I said: "Lord, what is found in greater amounts is sold more cheaply, but what is found rarely is of great value."

He answered and said to me: "Weigh for yourself what you have understood. What is found rarely gives greater joy to the one who has it than what is very plentiful [?]. So it is also with the creation I have promised. I will tell you this further: do not count yourself among those who have despised me, and do not be counted among those who are to be tormented. For the reward of your works is stored up before the Most High, and it will be revealed to you at the last time.

"Now concerning death, this is the teaching. The decree of the times goes out from the Most High: a person's death and the separation of the flesh from the soul. Then the soul returns to the one who sent it, to worship the glory of the Most High. It may be one of those who despised me, who did not keep the ways of the Most High, who despised his law and did not conform to the fear of him [?]. Then they and their souls shall not enter the treasuries. From then on they shall drink torment, grieving and sorrowful, in seven ways.

"The first way: because they despised the ways of the Most High. The second: because they can no longer repent and do good so that they might live. The third way: because they see before them the good reward, because they believed the promises of the Most High. The fourth way: because they see their own eternal torments. The fifth way: because they see the other souls, guarded by angels. The sixth way: because they see the torment that is now coming. The seventh way, which is greater than all the ways already mentioned: they melt away with shame, they are consumed [?] with disgrace, and they melt with fear. For they see the glory of the Most High, before whom they sinned during their life [?], and before whom they are to be judged at the last time.

"But for those who kept the ways of the Most High, this is the renewal [?] when they are to be separated from the vessels of corruption. As long as they stayed in this world, they served the Most High. They endured struggle with toil at all times, so that they might keep the law of the one who gave it to them. Therefore this is the account of their reward, in seven orders.

"Their first order is this: with their toil they strove to overcome the evil thoughts formed together with them, which would lead them astray from life to death. The second order: they see the [?] of the souls of the ungodly and the place of their torment. The third order: they hear the testimony of their Creator that in their life they kept the law in which they believed. The fourth order: they understand the rest which they now have, gathered in their treasuries. They rest in great quiet, guarded by angels, and await the glory of the last time. The fifth order: they rejoice that they have escaped the former corruption and will inherit incorruption. They see the narrowness and the fullness of their [?], from which they are to be set free. They will receive the joy of spaciousness and become immortal. The sixth order: it is shown to them how their faces are to shine like the sun, and how the light of their incorruption is to be like the stars. The seventh order, which is greater than all those mentioned: they boast openly, and are comforted with confidence [?], and rejoice without shame. For they hasten to see the face of him whom they served in their life, by whom they will be glorified and from whom they will receive their reward.

"These are the orders of the souls of the righteous, which are now announced. But those of the former way, who despised justice, are scourged and suffer."

I answered and said: "Are the souls that leave their bodies given time to see all these things you have spoken of?"

He answered and said: "They are free for seven days. During those seven days they see the things just described, and only then are they gathered into their treasuries."

I answered and said: "If I have found favour in your eyes, show this also to your servant. On the day of judgment, will the righteous be able in any way to intercede before the Most High for the ungodly? Or fathers for their children, or children for their parents? Or brothers for brothers, or relatives for relatives, or acquaintances for those dear to them?"

He answered and said to me: "Since you have found favour in my eyes, I will make this known to you too. The day of judgment is decisive, and it will show the seal of truth. Look at how things are now. A father cannot send his son in his place, nor a son his father, nor a master his slave, nor a friend someone dear to him. None can send another to be sick in his place, or to die, or to eat, or to be glorified in his place. In the same way, then no one will be able to intercede for another, and no one will be able to harm another. For then each person shall bear their own justice."
I answered and said: How then do we find it written that Abraham first prayed for the people of Sodom, and Moses for the people who sinned in the wilderness,
and Joshua son of Nun for Israel, and Samuel in the days of Saul,
David for the plague on the people, and Solomon for the sanctuary,
and Elijah for rain and for the raising of the dead,
and Hezekiah for the city and the people in the days of Sennacherib; and many prayed for many.
So if now, when corruption has sprung up, the righteous have prayed for the ungodly, why will it not be the same hereafter?
He answered and said to me: Because the end of this world has not yet come, and the eternal glory of God has not yet been revealed, the mighty prayed for the ungodly.
But the day of judgment is the end of these times and the beginning of the world to come. It is the time of immortality, in which corruption has passed away,
sin has been destroyed, falsehood has vanished, righteousness has been revealed and truth has sprung up. And our faces have become blacker than darkness.
What use is this life of ours, since we have sinned and do not know what suffering awaits us?
He answered and said to me: These are the thoughts of this world: whoever is born on earth must always struggle.
If he is defeated, he will suffer what I have said; but if he overcomes, he will receive what I have promised.
For this is the way that Moses taught while he was still alive, when he said to the people: "Choose life, so that you may live."
But they did not believe him, nor the prophets after him, nor the one who sent the prophets.
Therefore there was no grief over their destruction like the rejoicing over the life of his own faithful.
I answered and said: I know, Lord, that the Most High [?] is called merciful toward those who have come into the world from eternity [?],
and gracious, showing mercy to those who turn to his law,
and patient with those who have sinned, as one who shows grace to his own works.
For he is ready to forgive their former deeds,
and he is greatly merciful, for he has multiplied his mercies all the more on this same world: for those who were disobedient and also for those who gave thanks.
If he had not multiplied his mercies, the world and its [?] inhabitants could not live.
He is a giver [?]. If he had not given out of his own goodness, and had not lightened the iniquities of those who do iniquity, how could the many myriads of the human race have been able to live?
He is also a righteous judge. If he did not pardon those created by his word, and instead wiped out this great multitude of the weakness of sinners,
not even one of those countless multitudes would remain.
He answered and said to me: The Most High made this world for the many, but the world to come for the few.

I will explain this parable to you, Ezra: ask the earth and it will tell you that earth is more plentiful where a man finds [it], and the place [?] is [small?] from whose soil gold comes out. So it is also with the affairs of this world.
Many have been created, but few will live.
I answered and said: Let my soul now rejoice in understanding, and let my ears grow rich with knowledge.
O mind, you came to hear, and you have heard. Be still, and now desire nothing more, for it has not been given to you; only a little knowledge has been given to us.

O Lord, if only you would command your servant and give me, [give?] us, a heart that brings forth seed and a cultivation of the mind from which fruit might be found, so that every corruptible being might be able to live and find the life of man.
For all of us together and alike have been made by your hands, as I said.

For you gave life at once when you formed the body in the womb and gave it limbs, and you protected what you had made from heat and water, and for nine months the one you created and made carries what you formed.
And your word protects it along with her, and afterwards the womb gives forth what was kept within it.
And you commanded the breast, among the members, to grow rich with milk.
Then you nourished your creature from the breast for a long time, and by your providence you had mercy on that fully formed body.
For you raised him by your righteousness, and taught him by your law, and gave him understanding by your knowledge,
and you put him to death as your creature, and give him life as your handiwork.
Now then, will you destroy man, your creature, made with so much labour and by your command, and ordained by you with hard labour? If so, why then did you make that man?
But now I will speak, above all, about everything you have commanded me, and about your people, for whom I grieve,
and about the inheritance for which I mourn, and the race of Jacob, for which I am troubled.
Therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them, for I see the stumbling of all the inhabitants of the earth.
But I have also heard from the law about the creation that is to come.
Therefore hear my voice, and give ear to the words of my mouth that I speak.
And he said: Lord, you who dwell from eternity to eternity, who move upon the highest heights, whose dwelling is in the upper airs,
whose throne cannot be overcome and whose glory is beyond understanding, before whom the hosts of angels stand in fear, whose words are turned into spirit and fire, whose word is firmly established,
whose providence is firm and whose command is fearsome, whose look dries up the abysses and whose wrath melts the mountains, and whose truth is attested!
Hear, Lord, the voice of your servant, give ear to the things spoken to you, and look upon my words.
For as long as I am in this life I will speak, and as long as I keep this understanding I will pray to you: do not look upon these sins of your people, but look upon the service of your people.
And do not consider the deeds of the lawless, but look upon those who all keep your promises through suffering.
Do not remember those who behave wickedly before you, but remember those who in goodness have believed in the fear of you.
Do not see fit to destroy those whose ways are like those of cattle; but look upon those who have been taught by the splendour of your law.
Do not be angry with those who are like evil wild beasts,
but remember the love of those who always hope in your glory.
For we and our forefathers have also persisted in the ways of corruption;
but you are merciful toward us sinners.
If you wish to have mercy on us fully, though we do not have such works, then your name will be called merciful.
For the righteous, whose works are before you, will receive a reward for their own works.
Or what is man, that you should not be angry with him? Or what is a corruptible race, that you should be so bitter toward them?
Truly, there is no one born of men who has not sinned against you.
Your goodness will be made known by this: when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works.
He answered and said to me: You have spoken rightly about everything, and it will be done according to these words of yours.
And truly I will not remember the deeds of sinners, nor their death, nor the judgement of their destruction;
but I will rejoice over the deeds of the righteous, for in this way comes their resurrection and their reward.
As you have said, so it is.

For a farmer sows much seed and plants many plants, but when the time for growing comes, not every seed sprouts and not every plant takes root. In the same way, not all those who are in this world will be saved.
I answered and said: If I have found favour before you, I would speak.
If the farmer's seed does not come up, it is because the rain did not fall on it, and it rots.
But man was made by your hands and resembles your image, just as the seed resembles the farmer.
Do not destroy them, Lord, but spare your people and have mercy on your inheritance, for you have pity on your own creation.
He answered and said to me: The things of this world are for this world [?]
For you fall far short of being able to love my creation more than I do. Yet you have many times counted yourself among the ungodly. Let it not be so!
For this reason too you were found wonderful before the Most High:
because you humbled yourself, for you counted yourself as nothing among the many, so that you might be glorified all the more.
But now the inhabitants of this world have been brought low by many miseries, because many have walked in pride.
But as for you, understand this, and seek glory for those who are like you.

For it is for you that paradise has been opened, and the tree of life has been planted, and the coming kingdom has been prepared, abundance has been prepared; and the place of rest has been built and prepared, and delight has been ordained from the beginning, and the tree of wisdom has sprung up.
Pain has been sealed away from you, death has been extinguished from you, hell has been hidden, corruption has fled.
Pains have passed away and been forgotten; he has revealed the full price of immortality.
Ask no more about the many who are destined for destruction,
for they too received freedom; yet they despised the Most High, and belittled his law, and abandoned his ways,
and, what is more, they trampled down his worthy ones.
They said in their heart, "There is no God"; for this reason they know their death.
Just as the good things that were spoken of await you, so the torment thirsts for them, for it has been prepared. And it is not that the Most High desires the destruction of human beings,
but rather that those who were sealed [?] have defiled the name of their Creator, and were not thankful to him who prepared good things for them.
But now, for this reason my judgment has drawn near,
which has not been made known to many, but only to you and to the few who are like you.
I answered and said: [?] You are going to perform many signs, but you have not told me about the last, or at what time it will be.
He answered and said to me: Measure it carefully yourself, and it will be, when you see that the sign of signs has passed,
then understand that it is the time in which [?] the created [?]
And when you see [?] in this world the quaking of places, evil plotting among the nations, instability among leaders, and trembling among rulers,
then understand that this is what the Most High spoke of in those former days.
Then everything that is to come [?] the beginning
The beginning is made known by portents and mighty acts, and the end by deeds and signs.
And then those who now have despised [?] this will be amazed
[?] was, they did not understand the way of long-suffering.
and for whom this world exists.
I answered and said:
As is [?], so also is its seed; and as is the flower, so also is its seed; and as the deeds were, so also is the judgment; and the laborer [?] his [?]. There were times before this [?].
when I was deliberating before the creation of this [world?] in which they dwell, and no one [?] me.
And then there was no one; and now they have been created upon the world and upon [?] unfailing [?] and law [?]
And I saw my world, and behold, it was lost.
I answered and said: I will speak before you, Lord.
Behold, I will go, as you have commanded me, and I will instruct the people who are now living. But those who are yet to be born, who will instruct them?
For this world lies in darkness, and its inhabitants are without light;
for your law has been burned, and because of this no one knows the things that have been done until now, or the things that are yet to be done.

If I have found favour before you, [send?] the Holy Spirit into me, and I will write down everything that has happened in this world from the beginning, what was written in your law, so that people may be able to find your places, and those who desire eternal life may seek out your ways.
He answered and said to me: Go and gather the people, and command them not to seek you for forty days.
And prepare many tablets at this time, and begin to write
And I went, as the Lord had commanded me, and I gathered all the people and said:
Hear, O Israel, these words:
Our fathers lived as strangers in Egypt, and they were delivered from there.
And they received the law of life, which they did not keep, and which you too have transgressed after them.
And Zion was given to you as an inheritance, but you and your fathers committed lawlessness and did not keep his ways, which he commanded you.
For the Most High is a judge of righteousness; he took away from you that exalted time.
And here you are, together with our brothers who are among you.

If you separate yourselves from your evil thoughts, and if your hearts are instructed, then you will keep the living and have mercy on the dead [?]. (35) For the judgment of death will come afterward, when you are made alive a second time; and the name of righteousness will be revealed, and the ungodly will be exposed.
But let no one come to us, and let no one seek me for forty days.
And I took five men with me, as he had commanded me, and we went out into the field and stayed there.
And on the next day, behold, a voice called me and said: Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink.
And I opened my mouth, and behold, he gave me a full cup; it was full of water, but its colour looked like fire.
And I took it and drank, and knowledge welled up from my heart, and wisdom spread through my breast, and my spirit kept remembering and was eager.
And my mouth was opened and was no longer shut.
And the Most High gave understanding to those five men, and they wrote down what was spoken, one after another, in signs that they did not know.
And I was there forty days. They wrote by day and ate bread at night, but I spoke all day and was not silent at night.
And in those forty days I wrote these ninety-four books.
And it came to pass, when the forty days were completed, that the Most High spoke to me and said:
"The twenty-four which you wrote first, set out openly and let the worthy read them,
but the seventy you shall keep hidden, so that you may give them to the wise among your people.

For in them is the fire of understanding, and the spring of wisdom, and the river of knowledge." So we spent [the time] in those seven years. In the fifth year from the creation, which is five thousand, on the twenty-fifth day of the third month, Ezra was taken up and was brought into the kingdom, to be with those like him.
